prompt: An ice-cream treat is a cone of radius $3$ in and height $10$ in, topped by a perfect hemisphere (half a ball) of ice cream with radius $3$ in. Write the exact total volume in terms of $\pi$ (for example, write $7\pi$ as 7pi).
hint: Two solids, two formulas, then add: cone $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$ and hemisphere (half of $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$).

hints.text: Two solids, two formulas, then add: cone $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$ and hemisphere (half of $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$).

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Do one solid at a time: a cone of radius $3$ and height $1$ alone holds $\frac{1}{3}\pi(9)(1) = 3\pi$. Once that step feels routine, redo it with height $10$ and then add the hemisphere.

explanation: Hemisphere: a full sphere is $\frac{4}{3}\pi(3)^3 = 36\pi$, and half of that is $18\pi$ cubic inches.
Add the two pieces: $30\pi + 18\pi = 48\pi$ cubic inches (about $150.8$).

alternativeExplanations.title: Handle one solid at a time
steps: Write "cone $=$" and "hemisphere $=$" on two separate lines before computing anything — composite solids go wrong when the work gets tangled.
Both pieces here share the same radius $3$, but only the cone uses the height $10$; the hemisphere is governed entirely by its radius.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The usual wrong answer is $66\pi$: using the FULL sphere formula, $36\pi$, instead of halving it for a hemisphere.

The word "hemisphere" means half a ball, so compute the sphere and then cut it in two: $36\pi \to 18\pi$. A quick check: the scoop on top should be smaller than the tall cone below it, and $18\pi < 30\pi$ ✓
